questions.qtext:
Consider the following original code segment:

\[ \begin{array}{l} x = 5 \\ x = x - 3 \\ \text{if } x < 3 \\ \quad y = x * 2 \\ \quad w = y \\ \text{else} \\ \quad y = x - 3 \\ w = x - y \\ z = x + y \end{array} \]

Which of the following represents the correct translation of the original code into SSA form?

options.text:
\[
\begin{array}{l}
\texttt{x\_1 = 5}\\
\texttt{x\_2 = x\_1 - 3}\\
\texttt{if x\_2 < 3}\\
\qquad \texttt{y\_1 = x\_2 * 2}\\
\qquad \texttt{w\_1 = y\_1}\\
\texttt{else}\\
\qquad \texttt{y\_1 = x\_2 - 3}\\
\texttt{w\_2 = x\_2 - y\_1}\\
\texttt{z\_1 = x\_2 + y\_1}
\end{array}
\]

\[

\texttt{w\_2 = x\_2 - y\_1}\\

\texttt{else}\\
\qquad \texttt{y\_2 = x\_2 - 3}\\
\texttt{w\_2 = }\Phi\texttt{(w\_1, 0)}\\
\texttt{y\_3 = }\Phi\texttt{(y\_1, y\_2)}\\

questions.solution:
Answer: D

Source solution 1 (score: 0)

$\textbf{Converting to SSA}$



$\Phi(y_1, y_2)$ is defined as $y_1$ if we arrive at this instruction through the THEN branch, $y_2$ if through the ELSE branch.

One needs to introduce $\Phi$ functions at every point of the program where several "paths'' merge.
